endorsements.title: CHAI AI governance frameworks (playbooks)
endorsements.quote: Flag validation gaps—particularly for high-risk clinical AI—as priority remediation items.

commentary.bottom_line: No study supplied for this map tests whether risk-tiered validation requirements and review routes lead to better-validated high-risk tools or less burden on low-risk ones. The recommendation currently rests on a single framework endorsement from the CHAI governance playbooks.

perspectives.view: Zero studies test the practice, and zero studies document the hazard. Under GRADE conventions, certainty cannot be rated above no direct evidence. The single supporting source is a framework statement, which reflects expert consensus and does not measure whether tiering changes validation quality, deployment decisions, or patient outcomes.

The CHAI governance playbooks carry this as a must-level item and direct committees to flag validation gaps in high-risk clinical AI as priority remediation. That endorsement gives committees a reference for their policy language. It does not establish which risk thresholds should trigger mandatory local validation, and no supplied study addresses that question.

commentary.research_gap: No supplied study compares risk-tiered validation routes with uniform validation or with no formal requirement. Useful designs would track, across health systems, how often high-risk tools reach deployment without local validation, how many performance problems local validation detects that vendor attestation missed, and how much reviewer time each tier consumes. A related question is how accurately committees assign tools to risk tiers in the first place.
commentary.underserved_note: No study tested the practice, so no evidence covers Medicaid, safety-net, limited English proficiency, or low-literacy populations. Vendor attestation and prior evidence may come from populations that differ from a safety-net system's patients, and the existing record gives no information on whether tiering rules account for that mismatch.
